old: Thermal interrupts occur when the local or remote temperature reading crosses a user-programmable high thermal limit or a low thermal limit. The THERM interrupt output signal can be cleared by reading the status register associated with the fault or by successfully responding to an ARA transmission by the master. In both cases, the thermal fault is cleared but is reasserted at the end of the next conversion if the fault condition still exists. The interrupt does not halt automatic conversions. The THERM output is open drain so that multiple devices can share a common interrupt line. All thermal interrupts can be masked using the THERM Mask register. Interrupt mode can be selected by writing bit 4 in the Configuration register to a 0.

- EN (Pin 2):** Connected to a voltage divider (R1, R2) from  $V_{IN}$ . The signal passes through a 0.4V reference and an internal reference block (providing 0.55V, 0.5V, and 0.49V references).
- MODE/SYNC (Pin 9):** Receives a square wave input and feeds into the MODE DETECT block and the OSCILLATOR.
- RT (Pin 10):** Connected to a resistor  $R_T$  and feeds into the OSCILLATOR.
- AGND (Pin 1):** Ground connection for the analog section.
- MODE DETECT:** Generates control signals for BURST, FORCED CONTINUOUS, and PULSE SKIP modes.
- OSCILLATOR:** Generates a clock signal for the SLOPE COMP and the S Q R flip-flop.
- SLOPE COMP:** Compares the oscillator signal with a slope to control the S Q R flip-flop.
- S Q R Flip-Flop:** Controls the SWITCH LOGIC AND ANTI-SHOOT THROUGH block.
- SWITCH LOGIC AND ANTI-SHOOT THROUGH:** Controls the power switches (MOSFETs) connected to the SW pin.
- BURST DETECT:** Monitors the output for burst mode conditions.
- PGND ( Pins 4, 7, and 13):** Ground connection for the power section.
- SW ( Pins 5, 6):** Output to the power switch node, connected to an inductor  $L$  and output capacitor  $C_{OUT}$ .
- FB (Pin 12):** Feedback pin connected to a resistor divider ( $R_A$ ,  $R_B$ ) from  $V_{OUT}$  to the error amplifier.
- PGOOD (Pin 11):** Output of a fault detection circuit (NAND gate) to a P-channel MOSFET.
- FAULT:** Output of a fault detection circuit (NAND gate) to a P-channel MOSFET.
- SS (Pin 14):** Source sense pin connected to a current sense resistor  $R_C$  and a capacitor  $C_{SS}$ .
- IC (Pin 15):** Input current sense pin connected to a current sense resistor  $R_C$  and a capacitor  $C_{SS}$ .
- IC (Pin 15):** Input current sense pin connected to a current sense resistor  $R_C$  and a capacitor  $C_{SS}$ .
new:
- **EN (Pin 2):** Connected to the R1/R2 (OPT) resistor divider from  $V_{IN}$ . EN drives the + input of a comparator with hysteresis whose – input is at 0.4V; the comparator output enables the INTERNAL REFERENCE block (0.55V, 0.5V and 0.49V outputs).
- **MODE/SYNC (Pin 9):** Shown driven by a square wave; feeds the MODE DETECT block (BURST, FORCED CONTINUOUS, PULSE SKIP outputs) and the OSCILLATOR.
- **RT (Pin 10):** Connected to a resistor  $R_T$  to ground and to the OSCILLATOR.
- **AGND (Pin 1):** Connected to ground.
- **OSCILLATOR:** Drives the S input of the S-R latch and the SLOPE COMP block.
- **Current loop:** SLOPE COMP and the sensed top-switch current are summed (+); the sum and  $V_C$  feed a comparator that drives the R input of the latch. The latch Q output drives the SWITCH LOGIC AND ANTI-SHOOT THROUGH block, which drives the top (P-channel) and bottom (N-channel) power MOSFETs through two drivers. The bottom-switch current is also sensed and fed back to the switch logic.
- **BURST DETECT:** Monitors  $V_C$  and drives the switch logic.
- **Error amplifier:**  $G_M$  amplifier with its – input on FB and two + inputs, 0.5V and SS; its output is  $V_C$ , compensated by  $C_{PAR}$  and  $R_C$  in series with  $C_C$ .
- **SS:** Soft-start node charged by current source  $I_{SS}$  into  $C_{SS}$  and discharged by an N-channel MOSFET driven by FAULT.
- **PGOOD (Pin 11):** Open-drain N-channel MOSFET driven by an OR gate (FAULT) of two comparators with hysteresis that compare FB with 0.49V and 0.55V.
- **V<sub>IN</sub> (Pins 3, 8):** Top-switch supply, bypassed by  $C_{IN}$ .
- **SW (Pins 5, 6):** Switch node, connected to the inductor  $L$  and the output capacitor  $C_{OUT}$  at  $V_{OUT}$ .
- **PGND (Pins 4, 7, and 13 (Exposed Pad)):** Bottom-switch return, connected to ground.
- **FB (Pin 12):** Connected to the  $R_A$ / $R_B$  divider from  $V_{OUT}$ , with  $C_{FF}$  across  $R_A$ .

The diagram illustrates the internal architecture of the LTC3313 buck converter. Key components and their connections are as follows:

- Power and Input:**  $V_{IN}$  is connected to the input pin and the internal reference.  $C_{IN}$  is connected to the input pin.
- Reference and Control:** The **INTERNAL REFERENCE** block provides 0.55V, 0.5V, and 0.49V references. The **EN** pin is connected to a voltage divider ( $R1_{OPT}$ ,  $R2_{OPT}$ ) and the reference. The **RT** pin is connected to a resistor  $R_T$  and the **OSCILLATOR**. The **MODE/SYNC** pin is connected to a resistor and the **OSCILLATOR**.
- Switching and Sense:** The **OSCILLATOR** drives an **S Q R** flip-flop, which feeds into **SWITCH LOGIC AND ANTI-SHOOT THROUGH**. This block controls the **SW** (Switch) and **PGND** (Power Ground) pins. **SENSE<sup>+</sup>** and **SENSE<sup>-</sup>** pins are connected to the output and input pins, respectively.
- Control and Error:** The **ERROR AMP** compares the **FB** (Feedback) pin voltage (0.5V) with a reference. The **SLOPE COMP** (Slope Compensator) is connected to the **FB** pin. The **FB** pin is also connected to a resistor divider ( $R_A$ ,  $R_B$ ) and a capacitor  $C_{FF}$ . The **AGND** (Analog Ground) pin is connected to ground.
- Temperature and Fault:** The **SSTT** (Supply Temperature) pin is connected to a capacitor  $C_{SS}$  and a temperature sensor. The **FAULT** pin is connected to a fault detector and a transistor. The **PGOOD** (Power Good) pin is connected to a transistor and a fault detector.
- Output:** The **SW** pin drives the inductor  $L$  and the output capacitor  $C_{OUT}$ . The **V<sub>OUT</sub>** is taken from the output node.
new:
The diagram illustrates the internal architecture of the LTC3313 buck converter. Key components and their connections are as follows:

- **EN:** Connected to the R1/R2 (OPT) resistor divider from  $V_{IN}$ . EN drives the + input of a comparator with hysteresis whose – input is at 0.4V; the comparator output enables the INTERNAL REFERENCE block (0.55V, 0.5V and 0.49V outputs).
- **RT:** Connected to a resistor  $R_T$  to ground and to the OSCILLATOR.
- **MODE/SYNC:** Drawn with a two-way arrow to a clock waveform (clock input or output) and connected to the OSCILLATOR.
- **Current loop:** The OSCILLATOR drives the S input of the S-R latch, whose Q output drives the SWITCH LOGIC AND ANTI-SHOOT THROUGH block. That block drives the top and bottom power MOSFETs through two drivers (the bottom driver is supplied from  $V_{IN}$ ). The current comparator has SENSE<sup>+</sup> (through a resistor) on its + input and SENSE<sup>–</sup> on its – input, and drives the R input of the latch. SLOPE COMP and the ITH voltage are summed (Σ) and the sum is connected to the + input node of the current comparator.
- **ERROR AMP:** Transconductance amplifier with its – input on FB and two + inputs, 0.5V and the SSTT node; its output is the ITH node, compensated externally by  $R_C$  in series with  $C_C$  (dashed connection).
- **SSTT:** Connected to the external capacitor  $C_{SS}$ , charged by a 10µA current source and pulled to ground by an N-channel MOSFET driven by FAULT. A buffer amplifier with  $V_{TEMP}$  on its + input and its output fed back to its – input also drives the SSTT node.
- **PGOOD:** Open-drain N-channel MOSFET driven by an OR gate (labeled FAULT) of two comparators with hysteresis that compare FB with 0.49V and 0.55V.
- **V<sub>IN</sub>:** Supply of the top switch and its driver, bypassed by  $C_{IN}$  to ground.
- **SW:** Switch node between the two MOSFETs, connected to the inductor  $L$ ; the output node  $V_{OUT}$  has the output capacitor  $C_{OUT}$  to ground.
- **PGND:** Source of the bottom MOSFET, connected to ground.
- **FB and AGND:** FB is connected to the  $R_A$ / $R_B$  divider from  $V_{OUT}$ , with  $C_{FF}$  across  $R_A$ ; the bottom of  $R_B$  is connected to AGND and to ground.
evidence: PDF p10 block diagram (render, 220 dpi crop): the AI bullet list had broken bold markers ('Power and Input:**'), invented a 'FAULT pin' (FAULT is an internal signal driving the SSTT pull-down and the OR gate output), called SSTT 'Supply Temperature' (PDF p9: Soft-Start, Track, Temperature Monitor), said MODE/SYNC was connected to a resistor, SENSE+/SENSE- were 'pins connected to the output and input pins', and SLOPE COMP was connected to FB (it is summed with ITH into the current comparator). It also omitted ITH, R_C/C_C, the 10µA source, the V_TEMP buffer and the 0.49V/0.55V PGOOD comparators. Rewritten from the drawing.

old: The diagram illustrates the internal architecture of the LTC3315A dual-buck converter. It features two parallel buck converter paths, BUCK1 and BUCK2. Each path includes a BUCK CONTROL block, a SWITCH LOGIC AND ANTI-SHOOT THROUGH block, and a switch driver stage consisting of two MOSFETs. The output of each buck converter is connected to an input pin (V<sub>IN</sub> 10, B1, D4 for BUCK1 and V<sub>IN</sub> 7, D1 for BUCK2) and a switch pin (SW1 11, C3, C4 and SW2 6, C1, C2). Feedback pins (FB1 2, A3 and FB2 3, A2) are connected to the output of each buck converter through a resistor and a transconductance amplifier (G<sub>M</sub>). The feedback loop for each buck converter includes a 0.5V reference and a 0.5V reference. The feedback signals are compared with 0.5V references and the outputs are combined with the enable signals (ENBUCK1 and ENBUCK2) using logic gates to control the switch drivers. The enable signals are derived from input pins EN1 (1, B3) and EN2 (4, B2) through 0.4V comparators. The mode detection block receives inputs from the mode/sync pin (12, A4) and the internal reference (0.55V, 0.5V, 0.49V, 0.4V) and outputs pulse skip, FC, and burst signals. The oscillator provides a 0° and 180° clock signal to the BUCK CONTROL blocks. An over temperature detect block monitors the temperature and provides an OT signal to the BUCK CONTROL blocks. The PGGOOD pin (5, A1) is connected to the output of a logic gate that combines the feedback signals and the enable signals. The ground pins (8, 9, 13) are connected to the exposed pad and the balls (B4, D2, D3).
new: The diagram illustrates the internal architecture of the LTC3315A (description written from the PDF drawing). EN1 (1, B3) and EN2 (4, B2) each go to a hysteretic comparator against 0.4V whose outputs are ENBUCK1 and ENBUCK2. MODE/SYNC (12, A4) goes to the MODE DETECTION block (outputs PULSE SKIP, FC, BURST) and to the OSCILLATOR. An OR gate of ENBUCK1 and ENBUCK2 enables the OSCILLATOR and the OVER TEMPERATURE DETECT block. The oscillator output drives BUCK1 at 0° and, through an inverter, BUCK2 at 180°; the OT signal goes to both BUCK CONTROL blocks. The INTERNAL REFERENCE block provides 0.55V, 0.5V, 0.49V and 0.4V. Each buck (BUCK1, BUCK2) contains a BUCK CONTROL block, a SWITCH LOGIC AND ANTI-SHOOT THROUGH block and two gate drivers for a PMOS high-side switch from V<sub>IN</sub> (with a current-sense element) and an NMOS low-side switch to ground, whose common node is SW. A G<sub>M</sub> error amplifier compares FB with 0.5V; its output V<sub>C1</sub>/V<sub>C2</sub> has an internal series R-C to ground and feeds BUCK CONTROL. BUCK1 uses V<sub>IN</sub> (10, B1, D4), SW1 (11, C3, C4) and FB1 (2, A3); BUCK2 uses V<sub>IN</sub> (7, D1), SW2 (6, C1, C2) and FB2 (3, A2). For power good, FB1 and FB2 each go to two hysteretic comparators (against 0.55V and 0.49V) whose outputs feed a NAND gate; each result is gated with ENBUCK1 or ENBUCK2 by a second NAND gate, and these two outputs and the OR of ENBUCK1/ENBUCK2 feed a final NAND gate that drives the gate of an N-channel open-drain transistor on PGOOD (5, A1). GND: pins 8, 9, 13 (exposed pad); balls B4, D2, D3.

In the PCB, θ<sub>CB</sub> resistors spread heat sideways on the top layer and on the bottom layer, on both sides, and θ<sub>VIA</sub> connects the top-layer and bottom-layer nodes under the package. old:
- 1) Place the device as close as possible to the thermal diode. In noisy environments, such as a computer motherboard, this distance is typically 10cm to 20cm. This length can be increased if the worst noise sources are avoided. Noise sources include displays, clock generators, memory buses, and PCI buses.
- 2) Do not route the DXP\_ and DXN\_ traces across fast digital signals, which can easily introduce +30°C error, even with good filtering.

- 3) Route the DXP\_ and DXN\_ traces in parallel and in close proximity to each other. Each parallel pair of traces should go to a thermal diode. Route these traces away from any higher voltage traces, such as +12V<sub>DC</sub>. Leakage currents from PCB contamination must be dealt with carefully since a 20MΩ leakage path from DXP\_ to ground causes approximately +1°C error. If high-voltage traces are unavoidable, connect guard traces to GND on either side of the DXP\_ - DXN\_ traces ([Figure 5](#)).

- 4) Route through as few vias and crossunders as possible to minimize copper/solder thermocouple effects.

The reset function is triggered on the SCL falling edge of the eighth bit of the least significant byte (Bit 0 of Frame 4 in [Figure 36](#)), and the AD5593R does not generate an ACK signal for this byte of data. The AD5593R has a $\overline{\text{RESET}}$ pin that performs the same function. For normal operation, $\overline{\text{RESET}}$ is tied high. A falling edge on $\overline{\text{RESET}}$ triggers the reset function. Both the hardware and the software reset functions take 250  $\mu$ s maximum and there must be no activity on the SCL pin of the AD5593R during this time.

old: The diagram illustrates the timing for serial read and write operations. It shows the relationship between the Serial Clock (SCLK), Chip Select (CS), Serial Data Input (SDI), Serial Data Output (SDO), and the output signal (OUTn). Key timing parameters include t<sub>1</sub> (SCLK period), t<sub>2</sub> (SCLK high/low time), t<sub>3</sub> (SCLK rise/fall time), t<sub>4</sub> (CS to SCLK), t<sub>5</sub> (SCLK to CS), t<sub>6</sub> (CS to SCLK), t<sub>7</sub> (CS rise/fall time), t<sub>8</sub> (SDI to SCLK), t<sub>9</sub> (SCLK to SDI), t<sub>10</sub> (CS to SDI), t<sub>11</sub> (SDO to SCLK), t<sub>12</sub> (SCLK to SDO), t<sub>13</sub> (CS to SDO), t<sub>14</sub> (SDI to SDO), and t<sub>OUT\_SYNC</sub> (SCLK to OUTn). The SDI line shows a sequence of R/W, A<sub>14</sub><sup>1</sup>, A<sub>13</sub><sup>1</sup>, A<sub>12</sub><sup>1</sup>, A<sub>0</sub>, D<sub>n</sub>, D<sub>n-1</sub>, ..., D<sub>1</sub>, D<sub>0</sub>. The SDO line shows a sequence of Z, D<sub>n</sub>, D<sub>n-1</sub>, ..., D<sub>1</sub>, D<sub>0</sub>, Z. The OUTn signal transitions at the end of the data sequence. A note states: <sup>1</sup>THESE BITS CORRESPOND TO THE DEVICE ADDRESSING (SEE DEVICE ADDRESSING SECTION).
new: The diagram (description written from the PDF drawing) shows SCLK, CS (drawn with an overbar), SDI, SDO and OUTn. CS is high for t<sub>10</sub> and then low for the whole frame; t<sub>4</sub> runs from an SCLK rising edge to the CS falling edge and t<sub>5</sub> from the CS falling edge to the first SCLK rising edge; t<sub>1</sub> is the SCLK period, t<sub>2</sub> and t<sub>3</sub> the SCLK high and low times; t<sub>6</sub> runs from the last SCLK rising edge to the CS rising edge and t<sub>7</sub> from the CS rising edge to the next SCLK rising edge. SDI carries X, R/W (W drawn with an overbar), A<sub>14</sub><sup>1</sup>, A<sub>13</sub><sup>1</sup>, A<sub>12</sub><sup>1</sup>, …, A<sub>0</sub>, D<sub>n</sub>, D<sub>n − 1</sub>, …, D<sub>1</sub>, D<sub>0</sub>, X, with data setup time t<sub>9</sub> and hold time t<sub>8</sub> around the SCLK rising edge. SDO is Z, then D<sub>n</sub>, D<sub>n − 1</sub>, …, D<sub>1</sub>, D<sub>0</sub>, then Z again; t<sub>14</sub> (SCLK falling edge to SDO enabled), t<sub>11</sub> (SCLK falling edge to SDO data available), t<sub>12</sub> (SCLK falling edge to SDO data remains valid) and t<sub>13</sub> (CS rising edge to SDO disabled) are marked. Timing parameters are defined as follows:  $t_{L1}$  is the time from the falling edge of LDAC to the start of the output transition;  $t_{L2}$  is the time from the falling edge of LDAC to the end of the output transition;  $t_{L3}$  is the time from the rising edge of LDAC to the start of the output transition; and  $t_{L4}$  is the time from the rising edge of LDAC to the end of the output transition. Stream Mode Register section). Looping allows the digital host to repeatedly read from or write to a set of registers as efficiently as possible.

If LOOP\_COUNT is set to 0, looping is disabled, and the following occurs:

- If the address direction is set to descending, the address decrements until it reaches Address 0x00. On the subsequent byte access, the address is set to the highest valued byte address available (0xFF).
► If the address direction is set to ascending, the address increments until it reaches the highest valued byte address available (0xFF). On the subsequent byte access, the address is reset to 0x00.

If LOOP\_COUNT is set to a value other than 0, looping is enabled, and the value in LOOP\_COUNT sets the number of bytes to be accessed in a single data phase before the byte address resets to the one specified in the instruction phase. The LOOP\_COUNT value must correspond to the number of actual bytes involved in the loop, which may differ from the number of registers addressed if some are multibyte registers.

The value of the LOOP\_COUNT bits can be kept or returned to the default value of 0 when the frame transaction is completed, that is, the CS is brought high. The LOOP\_COUNT behavior is controlled by the KEEP\_STREAM\_LENGTH\_VAL bit. If the user wants the programmed value to hold indefinitely, the user must first set the KEEP\_STREAM\_LENGTH\_VAL bit to 1 before programming the LOOP\_COUNT bits.

When using LOOP\_COUNT, be aware of the DAC update timings mentioned in the DAC Core Functions section. Additionally, while in streaming mode with LOOP\_COUNT > 0, the SCLK frequency must be configured with a minimum of 12.5MHz for the following conditions:

- SPI write to the INPUT\_CHn and MULTI\_INPUT\_CH registers while keeping LDAC low for the entire duration of the SPI frame.
► SPI write to and read back from the DAC\_CHn and MULTI\_DAC\_CH registers for the entire duration of the SPI frame.

old:
### Software Reset

The INTERFACE\_CONFIG\_A register includes two control bits, SW\_RESET and RESET\_SW used to initiate a software reset through the serial interface. Both bits must be set simultaneously within the same data phase to successfully trigger the reset. Once the software reset transaction is completed, the device performs a POR sequence followed by digital core initialization. All registers are reset to their default values, except for the INTERFACE\_CONFIG\_A register, which retains its current configuration.

### Power-On Reset (POR)

A POR signal is generated when the supply voltage first crosses the nominal threshold of 2.5V on AVDD. The POR resets the state of the user programmable registers if the supply voltage on AVDD drops below this threshold. On power-up, all registers are reset to their default values. Meanwhile, the POR circuit ensures that the output stages of all DAC channels are powered down (see the DAC Operating Modes section) until the output operating mode for the channel is changed.

### Hardware Reset

RESET is an active low signal that is low level triggered. Asserting RESET sets the device into the POR state. While RESET is asserted, all SPI transactions and LDAC pulses are ignored, and the SDO output is in a high-Z state. When the RESET is deasserted, the digital core initialization is performed, and all registers are reset to their default values.

The diagram illustrates the internal architecture of the LTC2975. Key components include:

- Power Regulators:** 3.3V and 2.5V regulators at the top left.
- Input Section:** Includes a 3R resistor, a 20Ω resistor, and a 350Ω resistor connected to the  $V_{IN\_SNS}$  pin.
- MUX:** A multiplexer that selects between various sense inputs ( $V_{SENSE0}$  to  $V_{SENSE3}$ ) and an internal temperature sensor.
- ADC:** A 16-BIT  $\Delta\Sigma$  ADC that receives signals from the MUX and a reference voltage.
- Reference:** A 1.232V (TYP) reference connected to the ADC and a 10-BIT DAC.
- DACs:** Two 10-BIT DACs and one 10-BIT DAC followed by a VBUF buffer.
- Memory:** EEPROM and RAM connected to an ADC\_RESULTS MONITOR LIMITS SERVO TARGETS block.
- Controller:** A PMBus ALGORITHM FAULT PROCESSOR WATCHDOG SEQUENCER that controls the overall system.
- Temperature Sensors:** Internal and external temperature sensors.
- Output Section:** Includes a MASKING block and an EXTERNAL TEMPERATURE SENSOR driver.

The diagram also shows the pinout for 58 pins, including power, ground, sense inputs, control pins, and temperature sensor inputs/outputs. Page markers for PAGE 0, PAGE 1, PAGE 2, and PAGE 3 are indicated on the right side.
